subject: Throughput slip on checkout path — request for availability window confirmation and evidence
messages:
From: Lara Shah <lara@nimblecart.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom@nimblecart.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Mar 2029 22:14:00 +0000
Subject: Checkout failures and sustained throughput drop (18 Mar 2029)

Hi Mina —

We saw a sustained degradation in checkout throughput between 2029-03-18 20:02:30 UTC and 2029-03-18 20:28:10 UTC. During that interval our checkout service recorded a spike in 429s and multi-second tail latency on tokenization calls. The impact was intermittent but long enough that ~8% of checkouts timed out and retried.

I've attached a small trace bundle with spans and our frontend logs (checkout_traces_20290318.zip). We're trying to understand whether this qualifies as an availability event under our contract and — if so — what the remedy path is. Can you confirm the window and let us know what evidence you need?

Tom and I are on standby if you want additional captures.

Thanks,
Lara Shah
Head of Engineering, NimbleCart
lara@nimblecart.com
Attachment: checkout_traces_20290318.zip (log bundle)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Lara Shah <lara@nimblecart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Mar 2029 01:07:42 +0000
Subject: Re: Checkout failures and sustained throughput drop (18 Mar 2029)

Hi Lara —

Thanks for sending the traces and the note. I'm sorry for the disruption — we take incidents like this seriously.

Immediate plan:
- I'll validate the exact request window you reported against our telemetry and confirm whether there was a regional throughput regression that meets the contractual availability definition.
- Ben (cc'd) will pull up per-shard serving metrics and the autoscaler events for the US-west pool.
- Please also forward any CDN/request IDs you have so we can cross-correlate (X-Req-Id / trace ids).

For evidence, our SLOs reference token-level availability over rolling 30-day windows. To evaluate eligibility for a remedy we'll need:
- The frontend traces you already attached (thank you).
- Any client-side retry logs and representative request IDs.
- The spans showing the 429s and any 5xxs.

We'll aim to confirm the adjudicated window and a proposed remedy path (if applicable) within 24 hours. If we determine it's credit-eligible we'll outline the calculation and provide a postmortem scope and timeline.

Quick question: do you have an internal estimate of revenue/checkout volume during that 26-minute window? If so, share a ballpark — it helps speed prioritization.

I will follow up once Ben has the metrics.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lara Shah <lara@nimblecart.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom@nimblecart.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Mar 2029 03:42:10 +0000
Subject: Re: Checkout failures and sustained throughput drop (18 Mar 2029)

Mina / team —

I pulled the serving and autoscaler logs for the US-west inference pool. Preliminary findings:
- At 2029-03-18 20:01:58 UTC we saw a short spike in queuing latency as a new deploy was finishing warmup; concurrent cold-starts on three dedicated workers coincided with a configuration mismatch where a previously applied batching profile was not active for model v2.1.
- The observed 429s line up with token emission backpressure; peak 429 rate at ~20:06:12 UTC. The window Lara reported (20:02:30 — 20:28:10 UTC) matches our telemetry for elevated error/latency.

Artifacts attached: inference_runtimes_20290319.csv (per-request latency and node-id), and I've added an internal raw trace index to the Drive link.

Credit eligibility note (preliminary):
- If we confirm a sustained regional throughput regression that materially impacted the customer's success path, this will likely meet the threshold for a proportional remedy under the SLA. Exact calculation will depend on the customer-configured capacity tier and the fraction of requests impacted.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Ask the customer for a short list of representative request IDs so we can pull full traces.
2) We'll produce a provisional impact window and a draft credit calculation by EOD (your timezone).
3) If credit-eligible, schedule a postmortem with engineering and ops to identify rollout and autoscaler fixes.

I'll attach the CSV to the ticket and link traces here once pulled.

— Ben
Ben Carter
SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachment: inference_runtimes_20290319.csv
From: Tom Nguyen <tom@nimblecart.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lara Shah <lara@nimblecart.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Mar 2029 10:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Checkout failures and sustained throughput drop (18 Mar 2029)

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- We've attached an expanded server-side log (nimblecart_server_logs_20290318.log) and a short list of request IDs below:
  - trace-id: nimble-7a3c2f1
  - trace-id: nimble-7a3c2f2
  - trace-id: nimble-7a3c2f8

- Estimated checkout volume during the window: ~11,400 requests; we see ~920 failed attempts (retries + client-side errors).

We appreciate the provisional assessment. Please escalate to the platform engineering on your side if there's an autoscaler or deployment rollback pattern that could have caused this — our payments peak is sensitive to small availability drops.

Also: if you can provide a short summary for our procurement team that includes the adjudicated window, whether it meets the SLA definition, and the next steps for remedy (credit calculation or otherwise), we'd like to include that in our internal incident brief.

Finally, we'd like the postmortem scoped to include: root cause, mitigation, timeline for the fix (configuration/automation), and a preventative plan to avoid similar warmup-induced regressions.

Lara / Tom — happy to jump on a quick call if needed.

— Tom
Tom Nguyen
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, NimbleCart
Attachment: nimblecart_server_logs_20290318.log
